video_title: KNICKS AREN'T SATISFIED 😤 Is New York's successful season at stake in the NBA Finals? | Get Up

quotes.speaker: Mike Greenberg
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Greenberg predicts the Knicks will reach the NBA Finals
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are going to the Finals, what do you think?
quotes.quote: I'm here today to tell you, after what we saw last night, Mr. Wilbon, that the Knicks have found the formula and the Celtics, for all of the great story that it is with Jayson Tatum coming back and everything, they reminded us. They're this team that plays with their food. They lose these ridiculous home games for no reason. The Knicks are going to the Finals, what do you think?

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins highlights the Knicks' roster depth and two-way players
quotes.excerpt: They have a closer and the best player in the Eastern Conference, Big Body Brunson is his name.
quotes.quote: One, they have a closer and the best player in the Eastern Conference, Big Body Brunson is his name. Karl-Anthony Towns is looking like a top-five big on both ends of the floor. And the most important thing that they have that you need to win a championship: a handful of two-way players. Al-a Josh Hart, OG Anunoby, Mikal Bridges, Landry Shamet, and I can even throw Deuce McBride in there now. When you see that togetherness, you see the way that they're coming together, playing agenda-free basketball. Big Mitchell Robinson, hey boy, I'm proud of you. Because he has been so locked in. Yes, they're going to continue to hack a Mitch, but the lobs, the block shots, his minutes that he come in, he's playing with so much spirit and passion. The Knicks are serious. If they get San Antonio, I got the Knicks picked to win in six. If they get Oklahoma City, it's going to the distance to seven, but I wouldn't be surprised if the Knicks pull it off.

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Wilbon explains how Western Conference series fatigue benefits the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Oklahoma City and San Antonio are going to Ali-Frazier each other.
quotes.quote: One thing to keep in mind, and I, the Knicks certainly can win this series. Part of this too is Oklahoma City and San Antonio are going to Ali-Frazier each other. People are going to need IVs and hospital stays, and then they're going to come into a series. And so yeah, the rest part, the rest versus rust won't matter because if the Knicks are starting in the West, okay, fine, if they're rusty part or all of Game 1, so what? We're not talking about starting off at Madison Square Garden having to play through that. So I, yeah, I think the Knicks very much can win this series.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel debates if the Knicks' season is already a success
quotes.excerpt: Is the Knicks season to date already a success or do you need to see them complete this?

text_blocks.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
text_blocks.text: Greeny, I got a question for you because you are a long-suffering New Yorker. Is the Knicks season to date already a success or do you need to see them complete this and win a championship before you deem this a success? If someone would have told you in October and said, deal or no deal, the Knicks make the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999 and that's where it ends, do you take that or do you take your chances?

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: I get so tired of people taking for granted how hard it is to make it to the NBA Finals, to get to the promised land. That's an accomplishment and a goal in itself. Yes, this is a success with the Knicks have done. I don't believe that they're satisfied. I'm huge on body language. If I walk up to you, I could test your energy and know if you like me or not. Nine times out of ten, you're going to love me because I'm a lover of a big guy. But my thing is, when I watched the postgame when they were getting crowned, getting their awards, they, they weren't celebrating like that. They weren't celebrating like that. And I said to myself, I said, you know what? They're ready.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: Here's the answer to your question. The answer to your question is what is the alternative to success? Because if the alternative to success is failure, then yes, it's a success. There's no way that this season can be a failure. I guess maybe if they get obliterated in the Finals, but I don't, I think that's so unlikely, I'm not even really putting it in the realm of possibility. If they play a representative series and lose to a really good San Antonio or Oklahoma City team, then yes, I think the season is a success. When it happens, you'll be disappointed, you're the fans, you've made this run, you feel like you're close, you feel like you have a chance. Obviously, it will be a disappointment. But if the opposite, if the alternative to success is failure, then this is by no, there is no circumstance in which this is a failure. Yes, it is a success.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins believes Jalen Brunson can become the greatest Knick ever
quotes.excerpt: You have a chance to be the greatest Knick ever.
quotes.quote: I did Jalen Brunson podcast, it all started breaking. I looked him in the eyes, I said, do you understand the moment? He was like, yeah. I said, no, no, no, no. Do you understand what's in front of you? You have a chance to make history. You have a chance to be the greatest Knick ever. You know why? Because the story matters. Don't come giving me this Frazier and all this stuff. No, no, no, no, no. Here's the thing. He joins the company of the small guards, al-a Isiah Thomas, Stephen Curry, for small guards to lead this. Jalen Brunson leads this team to win the NBA championship, he will be the greatest Knickerbocker ever.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Panel discusses Victor Wembanyama's fatigue and immense defensive responsibilities
quotes.excerpt: He's not the best player technically yet, but he is the face of the league internationally.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: Is there an element of maturing that we're seeing? I mean, something like, we overreact to every game because that's what the NBA is. After Game 4, San Antonio had played their way back into it. Now we're talking this morning like they've lost, which obviously they haven't. They still have a shot. But last night, just the way Wembanyama looked, I thought it was, if I'm a fan of theirs, it was alarming to the extent that it looked like he was trying and just didn't have it left to summon up.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: It's the first time all season he looked human. We talk about alien and all these things, which is complimentary. And Greeny, you said something I really find interesting about may get to be the face of the league. He's not the best player technically yet, but he is the face of the league internationally. It's interesting to talk to people who travel and they're overseas right now, basketball fanatics. You could be anywhere in Europe, Asia, Africa, Wembanyama is something they understand and are completely either fascinated with, obsessed by, but he, he looked human last night. And the question is, can he come up with two superhuman games against that team in two games, in two tries? He only gets two.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: Monica, let's start with one. Can he come up with one? Can he force a Game 7 when they head back home tomorrow night?

text_blocks.speaker: Monica McNutt
text_blocks.text: I do expect the Spurs and Wembanyama to force a Game 7, and it is because of the ebbs and flows of this series so far. The Thunder have not been as untouchable as we thought they were in the regular season in this postseason. And I think to me, you could look at the box scores through the series and be like, oh, they must have won the last game because the team that exerts the most effort to get the win looks flat to me in the next game. And I'm just not sure that the Thunder have solved that particularly with their injuries.

text_blocks.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
text_blocks.text: I think there's a point in every playoff season, I'm sure Wilbon can speak to this. There's a point in every playoff season where both teams know who the best team is, and the series starts to take its shape. San Antonio, I look at Dillon Harper, rookie, Sarr, young player, Stephon Castle, young player, Big Vic. This is their first time going through this. This is, you have fatigue, like me and Perk were talking about it in the hallway. Playoff basketball is more akin to wrestling than it is regular season basketball, and they are learning how fatigued, how fatiguing this is. Victor Wembanyama plays 10 more minutes a game in the playoffs than in the regular season, and he's supposed to be at peak optimal? No, I don't.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: And I'm going to add one thing. The emotions of it, which I know you can speak to, to to to be in an NBA locker room in the postseason. It is so quiet. There's just not the usual chatter and and socializing even among teammates who love each other. It is so exacting, right? And so emotionally, what I thought all season, Greeny, is, they're going to be great. Look, look, look. Victor Wembanyama is going to win championships plural with health, many maybe. But the emotion of going through this the first time and how tumultuous it is, I don't think they're up to that just yet.

text_blocks.speaker: Mike Greenberg
text_blocks.text: Not only that, but it feels to me, Big Perk, and maybe we can dive into this a little bit later this morning, his, you were, you were given an almost impossible assignment, guard Dwight Howard one-on-one. Wembanyama's is guard everyone. His assignment is basically, you guard all five guys. He's taking all five guys on the defensive side. He's expected to block every shot that comes in or at least alter every decision when guys want to come in, and he's defending on the perimeter.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: I agree. And we're to the point now where we're looking at the Spurs and we're saying, help a brother out offensively. Who, who is going to be that Robin? You can't ask Stephon Castle to guard SGA, the MVP, back-to-back MVP and put up buckets. But I'm going to say this real quick. The little things matter. Like if you're Miss Johnson, say if you're going to San Antonio and I believe that they're going to get Game 6, right? Right after Game 6, the Thunder jet is going to be on the runway. The Spurs need to have their jet ready as well. Like, you fly out that night. Yeah, you fly out that night, not the next day. It's little things that that add up. Like not flying in the day before, getting in that evening at 6:00 and then all, no, no, no, no. They leave, we leaving. Like that type of thing matters and people may say, oh, Perk, it's a dumb thing. No, it's a real thing. Because we've, we've done it. You got to put yourself at an advantage or put yourself in position the best way possible to be successful.
